subject: Control-plane connectivity regressions after private VPC upgrade — Acme Financial
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Thomas <eric.thomas@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T13:02:00Z
Subject: Control-plane connectivity incident — Acme Private VPC (us-east-1)

Eric —

I want to let you know we observed a drop in control-plane connectivity for your Private/VPC deployment in us-east-1 during a rolling control-plane upgrade we initiated at ~12:45 UTC. You likely saw API errors (503 / connection failure) for approximately 18 minutes; our telemetry shows a spike in failed API handshakes between 12:47–13:05 UTC.

Immediate actions taken: 
- Rolled back the control-plane to the previous stable revision at 13:06 UTC.
- Disabled the new feature-flag set that was part of the release.
- Collected debug logs and a diagnostic snapshot (attached).

We’re investigating root cause now and I’ve looped in Neha (CS) and Michael (infra) to coordinate. I’m very sorry for the disruption — I know this affected some production traffic. We’ll follow up with a timeline, root cause, and remediation plan by our postmortem (target: 2026-07-15).

Can you confirm you saw the issue and whether any downstream jobs were impacted beyond the control-plane (we want to capture any missed SLA-related events)? If you prefer a quick call, I can set one up within the hour.

Attachments: diagnostic_snapshot_20260712.zip (log bundle, 18MB)

— Rachel
Rachel Kim

Thanks Rachel.

Yes — we saw elevated 503s and a few background reconciliation jobs timed out. Impact window on our side roughly 12:46–13:04 UTC; some alerting pages fired but were resolved after your rollback. Can you confirm how you plan to prevent this on future control-plane upgrades? Also need to understand whether this qualifies for an SLA credit.

-Eric

Date: 2026-07-12T14:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: Control-plane connectivity incident — Acme Private VPC (us-east-1)

Rachel / team —

Initial findings from the log bundle: during the orchestrated control-plane upgrade a new service-discovery path attempted a metadata query that returned an unexpected null payload; code path didn't tolerate a null and produced an NPE that caused connection stacks to fail while re-establishing long-lived control-plane sessions. This only triggered when a specific feature-flag combination (opt-in telemetry + new sd endpoint) was present — which matches the targeted configuration we pushed to Acme's VPC.

Mitigation taken (already applied): rollback the release and toggle the flag off. Further actions planned:
- Patch the NPE check and add defensive guards (INF-12984).
- Add a rollout safeguard in the upgrade orchestration to detect and stop progressive rollouts when handshake errors exceed threshold for 2 nodes.
- Add an automated smoke-check that validates control-plane session establishment for Private VPC customers before marking nodes healthy.

I’ll attach the debug trace in the postmortem. ETA for a tested patch: ~48 hours (we will not auto-redeploy without a canary window).

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Thomas <eric.thomas@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T15:10:00Z
Subject: Postmortem & remediation plan — control-plane regression (Acme Private VPC)

Eric —

Apologies again for the incident on 2026-07-12. Attached is the formal postmortem and remediation plan (postmortem_acme_20260715.pdf). Key points: 

What happened:
- At 12:45 UTC we started a rolling control-plane upgrade targeting private control-plane components in us-east-1.
- At 12:47 UTC several nodes failed to re-establish control-plane sessions due to a null-pointer regression in the service-discovery path when telemetry metadata was present.
- Impact window observed: 12:46–13:05 UTC.

Root cause:
- A code regression introduced in release 2026.07.12 removed a defensive null-check around a new metadata response; with telemetry enabled in some Private VPC configs the null flowed through and caused an NPE during session handshake.

Remediation completed:
- Rolled back the upgrade at 13:06 UTC (prevented further customer impact).
- Deployed a corrective patch to the release branch and validated in our canary cluster (2026-07-14).
- Added orchestration-level rollout gates: handshake health check + stop-on-error thresholds.

Planned preventative measures:
- Automated pre-upgrade smoke tests specific to Private/VPC: validate session establishment and simple control-plane RPCs.
- Strengthened code review checklist and added static analysis rule for suspicious null flows.
- Expanded canary coverage for Private/VPC owners for the first 24 hours of a release.

Customer impact & credits:
- We recognize this was a production-impacting event. Per our SLA we are evaluating the eligible credit and will follow up with the formal calculation. Neha will coordinate the credit paperwork and next steps.

Next steps / ask:
- Would you be available for a 30-minute review call to go over the postmortem and the revised upgrade plan? We can propose times on Monday or Tuesday next week.
- Please reply if you have any additional observations from your side (reconciliations, missed jobs) so we can include them in the RCA.

Attachments: postmortem_acme_20260715.pdf (6 pages), diagnostic_snapshot_20260712.zip

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Eric Thomas <eric.thomas@acme-fin.com>

Date: 2026-07-16T14:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Postmortem & remediation plan — control-plane regression (Acme Private VPC)

Thanks for the thorough postmortem. Appreciate the quick rollback and the patch follow-through. A few items: 

1) We will take you up on a postmortem review call — Monday 2026-07-20 at 15:00 UTC works for my team.
2) Please confirm the SLA credit calculation and timeframe for the offset.
3) We’d like written assurance that future control-plane upgrades will include the handshake smoke test and stop-on-error gate before our next scheduled maintenance window.

Looking forward to the call.

-Eric
